summary: Practise construction scheduling, site progress tracking, and handover controls. Explore the five-day course and its practical work outputs.
lede: Managing construction projects means connecting scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, and delivery interfaces to work crews can execute and document. For site engineers, project coordinators, supervisors, and planners, the course develops practical controls for defining work packages, sequencing activities with Critical Path Method logic, and tracking installed quantities. You also practise maintaining lookahead plans, RFI and change logs, constraint records, and quality, safety, and handover evidence for site progress reporting.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course suits professionals who coordinate building and infrastructure delivery or supply project information to site teams. It is designed for construction practitioners who need working methods for field coordination, records, and progress reporting.
modules: CPM Schedule Logic and Lookahead Plans
prerequisites: No formal project-management qualification is required. Familiarity with construction sites, building or infrastructure work, or project documentation will help you apply the exercises. Coding is not required.
